page: Amazon Web Services hpc7a.24xlarge is a dedicated high-performance computing instance built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by AMD EPYC 9R14 processors. The instance delivers 48 physical x86_64 cores without simultaneous multithreading, running at 3.7 GHz with dedicated core allocation. Cache topology comprises 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. Memory configuration includes 768 GB of DDR5 operating at 5 GHz, providing a generous 16 GB of system RAM per core. The instance provides 300 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth and contains no bundled local storage or discrete graphics processing units.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate high throughput across memory and compute subsystems. Multi-core compute performance sits in the top 10% in stress-ng evaluations, corroborated by top-tier results in Clang compilation and PassMark physics testing. The 5 GHz DDR5 configuration achieves top-tier results in large-block uncached memory bandwidth, reaching 695.05 GB/s in reads and 347.3 GB/s in writes. Vectorized operations are supported through native AVX-512 extensions including VNNI and BF16, which directly underpin its strong results in small and medium parameter language model token processing.

From an infrastructure perspective, hpc7a.24xlarge trades bundled local storage for massive interconnect speed and raw memory density. Because zero local disk capacity is provided, applications require external network storage volumes or distributed file systems. The high 16:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio and dedicated non-hyperthreaded physical cores offer predictable computational execution, avoiding multi-tenant resource contention.

This hardware profile is suited for tightly coupled high-performance computing, large-scale computational fluid dynamics, structural simulations, physics modeling, memory-resident analytics, and distributed compilation pipelines requiring high memory bandwidth alongside 300 Gbps networking.
description: Amazon Web Services hpc7a.24xlarge is an x86_64 high-performance computing instance powered by AMD EPYC 9R14 processors on the AWS Nitro System. It provides 48 dedicated physical cores clocked at 3.7 GHz with simultaneous multithreading disabled, paired with 768 GB of high-speed 5 GHz DDR5 memory, achieving 16 GB per core. The instance includes 300 Gbps of baseline networking bandwidth, with no local storage or GPUs included. Benchmark results place hpc7a.24xlarge in the top 10% for multi-core stress-ng workloads, Clang compilation, PassMark physics simulation, and uncached large-block memory read and write operations. The platform features native AVX-512 extensions, yielding strong vector instruction performance. Because storage relies entirely on external volumes, the instance optimizes for memory bandwidth and low-latency network interconnects. It is designed for computational fluid dynamics, finite element analysis, distributed physics simulations, software compilation, and large in-memory data processing pipelines.
